item.title: CT to close transfer station at center of local trash dispute
item.description: The Torrington facility was the subject of a dispute involving two trash haulers and allegations of favoritism at the state Capitol.

item.title: CT department says it cannot comply with DCF, homeschool proposal
item.description: The bill would require that schools alert the education department when kids are withdrawn for homeschooling so it could then notify DCF.

item.title: CT’s chance to align juvenile sentencing with science
item.description: The United States remains the only country in the world that still permits children to be sentenced to life in prison.

item.title: How the war in Iran is impacting home energy costs in CT
item.description: The increase in oil costs is particularly harmful to low income families who rely on fuel and energy assistance programs to stay warm.

item.title: EMS workers ask to be included in Lamont’s free tuition proposal
item.description: The governor's bill offers help with college tuition and mortgage payments to firefighters and police. EMS workers want to be included.

item.title: CT lawmakers seek to rein in Trump on Iran
item.description: After Trump officials briefed Congress on the Middle East, Senate will take up war powers resolution Wednesday. House to follow Thursday.

item.title: Will CT recoup $127M in taxes owed by Prospect Medical Holdings?
item.description: At a ribbon-cutting at Waterbury Hospital Wednesday, Gov. Lamont said it’s unclear how much in unpaid taxes CT will recover from Prospect.

item.title: CT high school students argue for increase in ECS funding formula
item.description: Students from across CT urged lawmakers to act on two bills that would increase the Education Cost Sharing grant formula that funds schools.

item.title: A difficult week for Sen. Doug McCrory and earmarks
item.description: The FBI investigation of the Hartford Dem's role in delivering millions in earmarks played a part in Lamont’s line-item veto of the earmarks.

item.title: CT can lead on housing by confronting corporate consolidation
item.description: During the debate on HB 8002, critics argued that private equity posed a serious risk. I agree, but concern without action is not leadership.
